Prove all-field rank formula for biforms with one polynomial top coefficient (#217)

## New mathematical result

For any field K, a >= 2, 1 <= e < b, and f(x,z) = c_0 + ... + c_(e-1)
z^(e-1) + w(x) z^e with nonzero constant c_0, constant lower
coefficients, and nonzero deg(w)=d<a, the literal full cyclic-source
biform matrix satisfies

    rank R_(a,b)(f) = ab + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b, d floor((a+j)/e)).

This holds in every characteristic, with no additional coefficient
guard. In particular, it handles the genuine three-term non-diagonal
f=1+z+(1+x^d)z^2 and all e>=2. The proof parametrizes the e free
terminal polynomial coordinates, then establishes predictable degrees
using a residue-indexed triangular leading-coefficient matrix. It
retains every original source coefficient column.

## Evidence

- 900 exhaustive GF(2) and 1,836 exhaustive GF(3) full-source rank
comparisons;
- 216 deterministic GF(5)/GF(7)/GF(101) comparisons and 420 exact degree
witnesses;
- 24 separately implemented direct-coefficient SymPy/QQ ranks;
- three focused unittests, including an off-by-one mutation control,
passed locally.

Totals: 3,372 exact modular ranks plus 24 characteristic-zero checks,
all passing. Commands, code, pinned receipt and a precise continuation
record are committed. Local environment: Python 3.13.5 / SymPy 1.14.0.
Global repository regression and historical archive replay were not
completed in this run because the isolated public-network Pyroam runner
returned an internal error; hosted current-head required CI remains
mandatory.

## Claims and dependencies

Adds AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 with status
**proof-written-unreviewed**, independent_review=false,
improves_omega=false. Credits original literal source convention (pinned
source blob), preceding affine-z result #209 at its exact head, and
distinct #171/#186/#207 research. No unmerged runtime dependency or
external theorem is imported. Both archived 2026-10-20 research
directories are untouched.

Concurrent consolidation #214 may change STATUS, PROVENANCE and the
claim ledger on main. Reconcile the new main and rerun all required
checks before any merge; do not silently overwrite its source records.

## Limitations

The theorem classifies *individual* biform source slices with constant
lower coefficients. General u(x)+z*v(x)+z^2*w(x) minimal indices,
compatible three-leg tensor maps, auxiliary cost, and a full asymptotic
exponent implication remain open. No arithmetic exponent improvement
below 9/4 or independent mathematical review is asserted.

**Do not merge** until current-head required CI passes, all review
discussions are resolved, and the claim proof is checked against the
exact stated family.

+# Exact ranks for biforms with one polynomial top coefficient
+
+October 23, 2026. Owner-directed AI-assisted research. Claim AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 is proof-written-unreviewed: this file provides a written proof and finite exact controls, not an independent mathematical review, a tensor target, or an exponent improvement.
+
+## Statement and coefficient convention
+
+Let K be any field, a >= 2, b >= 2, 1 <= e < b, and m = a+b-1. Consider
+
+    f(x,z) = c_0 + c_1*z + ... + c_(e-1)*z^(e-1) + w(x)*z^e,
+
+where c_s belongs to K, c_0 is nonzero, and w(x) is a nonzero polynomial of degree d < a. The coefficients below the highest z-power are constants; only the highest coefficient may depend on x.
+
+Define the literal cyclic-source coefficient matrix with rows (j,L), 0<=j<b and 0<=L<m; columns (H,r), 0<=H<m and 0<=r<a; and entry
+
+    R[(j,L),(H,r)] = coefficient of x^(H-j)*z^(L-r) in f.
+
+Out-of-range coefficients are zero. This is the full, untruncated source matrix used in the main-branch slice-rank discussion and PR #209.
+
+**Theorem.** Put q_j = floor((a+j)/e) for 0<=j<e. Then, over every field and every permitted choice of coefficients,
+
+    rank_K R_(a,b)(f) = a*b + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b, d*q_j).       (1)
+
+For d=0 the formula gives rank ab. Since sum_j q_j=a, when b>=d*ceil(a/e) the rank is exactly ab+ad. All statements hold without characteristic exceptions.
+
+For the genuinely three-term family f=1+z+(1+x^d)*z^2 with 1<=d<a and b>=3, (1) gives
+
+    rank = ab + min(b, d*floor(a/2)) + min(b, d*ceil(a/2)).
+
+For example, a=3,b=7,d=2 gives rank 27 and a=4,b=5,d=3 gives rank 30. These are neither binomial source slices nor diagonal polynomials f(xz). They do not construct compatible maps on three tensor legs.
+
+## Proof over an arbitrary field
+
+Only row groups L=0,...,a+e-1 can be nonzero, totaling (a+e)b active rows. Describe a linear dependence among those rows by polynomials
+
+    lambda_L(x) = sum_(j=0)^(b-1) lambda_(j,L)*x^j,
+    0<=L<=a+e-1,
+
+all of degree <b. Contracting against a column (H,r) reads the coefficient of x^H in
+
+    c_0*lambda_r + sum_(s=1)^(e-1) c_s*lambda_(r+s)
+                 + w(x)*lambda_(r+e).                           (2)
+
+Each expression in (2) has degree at most (a-1)+(b-1)=m-1. Because the literal matrix contains every H=0,...,m-1, the row dependence vanishes exactly when (2) vanishes as a complete polynomial identity for every r=0,...,a-1. In particular no highest-degree coefficient is dropped.
+
+The nonzero constant c_0 makes this a polynomial recurrence that can be solved backwards:
+
+    lambda_r = -(1/c_0)*(sum_(s=1)^(e-1) c_s*lambda_(r+s)
+                                + w*lambda_(r+e)),              (3)
+
+for r=a-1,...,0. Thus the e terminal polynomials lambda_a,...,lambda_(a+e-1) are freely chosen from K[x]. For j=0,...,e-1, define V_j by choosing terminal lambda_(a+j)=1 and all other terminal polynomials zero. These V_j form a free K[x]-basis of the complete polynomial solution module.
+
+Assume d>0. Each entry V_j(i) expands as a sum of paths from index i to terminal index a+j: a step of size s<e contributes the constant factor -c_s/c_0, while a step of size e contributes the polynomial factor -w/c_0. There can be at most q_j=floor((a+j)/e) size-e steps. Consequently every coordinate of V_j has degree at most delta_j=d*q_j.
+
+Write a+j=e*q_j+r_j with 0<=r_j<e. At coordinate i=r_j, the path with q_j size-e steps is the unique path attaining that number of polynomial steps: it consists entirely of size-e steps. Its leading coefficient is
+
+    (-lc(w)/c_0)^(q_j),                                    (4)
+
+which is nonzero. Every other path has fewer polynomial steps, so has degree strictly below delta_j. For every coordinate i>r_j, a path with q_j size-e steps would require a total step length at least e*q_j > a+j-i. Such a path cannot occur, so the degree-delta_j coefficient is zero. If q_j=0, the same statements hold because r_j=a+j is a free terminal coordinate, with V_j(r_j)=1 and V_j(i)=0 for all i>r_j.
+
+The residues r_j form a permutation of 0,...,e-1. Restrict the leading coefficient vector of each V_j at degree delta_j to the first e row-group coordinates. After ordering the columns by r_j, these vectors form a triangular e-by-e matrix with nonzero diagonal (4), because the entries with i>r_j vanish. Therefore the degree-delta_j leading coefficient vectors of all V_j are linearly independent over K, even in positive characteristic.
+
+For any polynomials P_j, not all zero, linear independence prevents cancellation at the largest weighted degree:
+
+    deg(sum_j P_j*V_j) = max_(j:P_j != 0)(deg(P_j)+delta_j),  (5)
+
+where degree of a polynomial vector means the maximum of its coordinate degrees. Thus all coordinates of the sum have degree <b if and only if each P_j separately satisfies deg(P_j)<b-delta_j. The active-row kernel therefore has dimension
+
+    sum_(j=0)^(e-1) max(0,b-d*q_j).                        (6)
+
+If d=0, all recurrence coefficients are constants and all V_j are constant vectors. Their terminal coordinates form the identity, so they remain independent and (5)-(6) hold with delta_j=0.
+
+Subtracting (6) from the (a+e)b active rows gives
+
+    (a+e)b - sum_j max(0,b-d*q_j)
+    = ab + sum_j min(b,d*q_j),
+
+proving (1). Write a=e*k+r, 0<=r<e. Exactly r of the q_j equal k+1 and the rest equal k; hence sum_j q_j=e*k+r=a. This proves the corollary. QED.
+
+## Reproduction and scope
+
+The standard-library verifier builds the entire bm-by-am source matrix and determines its rank by exact modular Gaussian elimination, without using the recurrence. Completed controls: 900 exhaustive GF(2) cases across 27 shapes; 1,836 exhaustive GF(3) cases; 216 fixed-seed GF(5), GF(7), GF(101) cases; and 420 degree witnesses. All 3,372 agree with (1). The independently implemented coefficient-lookup matrix and exact SymPy rational elimination agree in 24 QQ cases. These are same-session software controls, not independent mathematical review.
+
+From the repository root:
+
+    python -I research/ai/2026-10-23-top-coefficient-biforms/verify.py --receipt results/local/top-coefficient-biforms.json
+    python -I research/ai/2026-10-23-top-coefficient-biforms/verify_charzero.py
+    python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_top_coefficient_biforms.py -v
+
+The literal source indexing and preceding affine-z classification are credited to the pinned main source and PR #209. PR #171 covers binomials, #186 the general gap and another special family, and #207 the diagonal f(xz) Toeplitz family. No unmerged proof is imported. This theorem concerns one free polynomial coefficient; it does not claim a classification of arbitrary quadratic-in-z coefficients or a matrix multiplication exponent below 9/4.
+
+The next open bottleneck is the two-nonconstant-coefficient polynomial recurrence for arbitrary u(x)+z*v(x)+z^2*w(x). With a nonconstant coefficient at lambda_r, the backwards solution (3) may cease to exist in K[x]; the minimal polynomial indices must then be determined. A three-leg tensor target, auxiliary costs, and a full asymptotic argument are also still missing.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent literal-source finite-field check of the top-coefficient biform rank theorem.
+
+Uses only the Python standard library. The rank oracle builds the complete
+coefficient matrix, including its zero rows, rather than using the syzygy proof.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import json
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def coefficient_matrix(a: int, b: int, e: int, c: tuple[int, ...], w: tuple[int, ...], p: int):
+    """The literal R_(a,b) rows (j,L), columns (H,r)."""
+    assert a >= 2 and b > e >= 1 and len(c) == e and len(w) == a
+    m = a + b - 1
+    M = [[0] * (a * m) for _ in range(b * m)]
+    # Build from source coefficients directly, never from the recurrence.
+    for r in range(a):
+        for j in range(b):
+            for s, coefficient in enumerate(c):
+                row = j * m + (r + s)
+                col = j * a + r  # column index is actually H*a+r; H=j.
+                M[row][col] = (M[row][col] + coefficient) % p
+            for k, coefficient in enumerate(w):
+                if coefficient:
+                    row = j * m + (r + e)
+                    col = (j + k) * a + r
+                    M[row][col] = (M[row][col] + coefficient) % p
+    return M
+
+
+def exact_rank_modp(M: list[list[int]], p: int) -> int:
+    A = [row[:] for row in M]
+    nrows = len(A)
+    ncols = len(A[0])
+    rank = 0
+    for col in range(ncols):
+        pivot = next((i for i in range(rank, nrows) if A[i][col] % p), None)
+        if pivot is None:
+            continue
+        A[rank], A[pivot] = A[pivot], A[rank]
+        inv = pow(A[rank][col] % p, -1, p)
+        A[rank][col:] = [(x * inv) % p for x in A[rank][col:]]
+        for i in range(rank + 1, nrows):
+            multiplier = A[i][col] % p
+            if multiplier:
+                A[i][col:] = [(x - multiplier * y) % p for x, y in zip(A[i][col:], A[rank][col:])]
+        rank += 1
+        if rank == nrows:
+            break
+    return rank
+
+
+def predicted_rank(a: int, b: int, e: int, w: tuple[int, ...], p: int) -> int:
+    deg = max(k for k, coeff in enumerate(w) if coeff % p)
+    return a * b + sum(min(b, deg * ((a + j) // e)) for j in range(e))
+
+
+def verify(a, b, e, c, w, p):
+    expected = predicted_rank(a, b, e, w, p)
+    got = exact_rank_modp(coefficient_matrix(a, b, e, c, w, p), p)
+    if expected != got:
+        raise AssertionError(f"R({a},{b}) e={e}, c={c}, w={w} over F_{p}: expected {expected}, got {got}")
+    return expected
+
+
+def xorshift32(x):
+    x ^= (x << 13) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    x ^= x >> 17
+    x ^= (x << 5) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    return x & 0xFFFFFFFF
+
+
+def run():
+    counts = Counter()
+    shapes = set()
+    observed = set()
+    # All lower coefficients and all nonzero top polynomials, over F_2.

+                                continue
+                            verify(a, b, e, c, w, 3)

+    rng = 0xB1F0A26E

+                        rng = xorshift32(rng)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent characteristic-zero oracle: direct definition and SymPy QQ elimination."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from fractions import Fraction
+from sympy import Matrix, Rational
+
+
+def rank_by_definition(a, b, e, c, w):
+    m = a + b - 1
+    poly = {(0, s): Rational(v) for s, v in enumerate(c) if v}
+    poly.update({(i, e): Rational(v) for i, v in enumerate(w) if v})
+    rows = []
+    for j in range(b):
+        for L in range(m):
+            rows.append([poly.get((H - j, L - r), 0)
+                         for H in range(m) for r in range(a)])
+    return Matrix(rows).rank()
+
+
+def expected(a,b,e,w):
+    d = len(w)-1
+    while d > 0 and w[d] == 0:
+        d -= 1
+    return a*b + sum(min(b, d*((a+j)//e)) for j in range(e))
+
+
+def run():
+    # Includes non-monic coefficients, fractions, and nonconstant middle-free cases.
+    checks=0
+    for a in (2,3):
+        for e in (2,3):
+            for b in (e+1,e+3):
+                for variant in (0,1,2):
+                    c = [Rational(2,3)]
+                    for k in range(1,e):
+                        c.append([Rational(0),Rational(-1,2),Rational(3,5)][(k+variant)%3])
+                    w = [Rational(1,7) if variant else Rational(0)]*a
+                    w[0] = Rational(1,7)
+                    w[min(a-1,variant)] = [Rational(2,5),Rational(-7,3),Rational(9,4)][variant]
+                    r = rank_by_definition(a,b,e,c,w)
+                    want=expected(a,b,e,w)
+                    assert r==want,(a,b,e,variant,r,want)
+                    checks += 1
+    return {'result':'PASS','charzero_QQ_cases':checks,
+            'oracle':'SymPy rational rank of full row-by-column coefficient matrix built from biform dict'}
+
+
+if __name__=='__main__':
+    print(json.dumps(run(),indent=2))

pulls.title: Prove all-field rank formula for biforms with one polynomial top coefficient
pulls.body:
## New mathematical result

For any field K, a >= 2, 1 <= e < b, and f(x,z) = c_0 + ... + c_(e-1) z^(e-1) + w(x) z^e with nonzero constant c_0, constant lower coefficients, and nonzero deg(w)=d<a, the literal full cyclic-source biform matrix satisfies

    rank R_(a,b)(f) = ab + sum_(j=0)^(e-1) min(b, d floor((a+j)/e)).

This holds in every characteristic, with no additional coefficient guard. In particular, it handles the genuine three-term non-diagonal f=1+z+(1+x^d)z^2 and all e>=2. The proof parametrizes the e free terminal polynomial coordinates, then establishes predictable degrees using a residue-indexed triangular leading-coefficient matrix. It retains every original source coefficient column.

## Evidence

- 900 exhaustive GF(2) and 1,836 exhaustive GF(3) full-source rank comparisons;
- 216 deterministic GF(5)/GF(7)/GF(101) comparisons and 420 exact degree witnesses;
- 24 separately implemented direct-coefficient SymPy/QQ ranks;
- three focused unittests, including an off-by-one mutation control, passed locally.

Totals: 3,372 exact modular ranks plus 24 characteristic-zero checks, all passing. Commands, code, pinned receipt and a precise continuation record are committed. Local environment: Python 3.13.5 / SymPy 1.14.0. Global repository regression and historical archive replay were not completed in this run because the isolated public-network Pyroam runner returned an internal error; hosted current-head required CI remains mandatory.

## Claims and dependencies

Adds AI-TOP-COEFFICIENT-BIFORM-RANK-001 with status **proof-written-unreviewed**, independent_review=false, improves_omega=false. Credits original literal source convention (pinned source blob), preceding affine-z result #209 at its exact head, and distinct #171/#186/#207 research. No unmerged runtime dependency or external theorem is imported. Both archived 2026-10-20 research directories are untouched.

Concurrent consolidation #214 may change STATUS, PROVENANCE and the claim ledger on main. Reconcile the new main and rerun all required checks before any merge; do not silently overwrite its source records.

## Limitations

The theorem classifies *individual* biform source slices with constant lower coefficients. General u(x)+z*v(x)+z^2*w(x) minimal indices, compatible three-leg tensor maps, auxiliary cost, and a full asymptotic exponent implication remain open. No arithmetic exponent improvement below 9/4 or independent mathematical review is asserted.

**Do not merge** until current-head required CI passes, all review discussions are resolved, and the claim proof is checked against the exact stated family.
